sentences.text: Almadasuchus is an extinct crocodylomorph, a member of the superorder that includes modern crocodiles, discovered in Patagonia, Argentina.
The genus contains only one known species, Almadasuchus figarii, known from a holotype — the specimen the species is based on — that preserves a posterior skull region and other bones.
Pol et al. described the genus and named the species in 2013 from fossils found in the early Late Jurassic Puesto Almada Member of the Cañadón Calcáreo Formation.
The quadrate connects to the basisphenoid and exoccipital bones, which likely made its skull completely akinetic, or immovable.
This animal lived during the Oxfordian stage, approximately 161.5 to 159 million years ago.
